$comment: England & Wales, Land Law, actual occupation as an overriding interest in registered land. Boland's original 1980 House of Lords judgment could not be fetched directly - BAILII returned HTTP 403, treated as final per docs/OPERATING_RULES.md; the judgment also predates Find Case Law's coverage. Verified instead via a later citing judgment, plus a direct fetch of the current statutory successor provision from legislation.gov.uk.
verification_method: Find Case Law direct fetch of a later citing judgment, plus a direct legislation.gov.uk fetch of the current statutory text. BAILII's own 1980 judgment text was not independently read this session.

authorities.name: Williams & Glyn's Bank Ltd v Boland
authorities.citation_note: The same fetched source rendered this elsewhere as '[1984] 1 AC 487' in its own text - almost certainly a garble of 1981, not an independent confirmation of a different year. [1981] 1 AC 487 is used here as the more plausible value, not asserted with full confidence.
authorities.date_note: Recorded as 1980 per secondary confirmation and the citing judgment's discussion; not independently confirmed via BAILII or Find Case Law this session (predates Find Case Law's coverage; BAILII blocked).
authorities.proposition: A spouse or beneficiary with a beneficial interest in a home who is in actual occupation at the relevant time holds an interest capable of overriding a registered disposition, regardless of the purchaser's or mortgagee's lack of notice - 'actual occupation' is to be given its ordinary factual meaning. Originally decided under s.70(1)(g) Land Registration Act 1925.
authorities.verification_note: Not read directly - BAILII blocked (HTTP 403) and the judgment predates Find Case Law's coverage. Confirmed via Link Lending Ltd v Bustard [2010] EWCA Civ 424 (below), fetched live.

authorities.name: Link Lending Ltd v Bustard
authorities.date_note: Year only confirmed; exact date not independently verified this session.
authorities.proposition: Treats Boland as good, current authority thirty years on, and discusses both s.70(1)(g) Land Registration Act 1925 and its successor, Schedule 3 paragraph 2 Land Registration Act 2002, as the old and new statutory homes of the same actual-occupation principle.

authorities.name: Land Registration Act 2002, Schedule 3, paragraph 2
authorities.proposition: The current statutory successor to s.70(1)(g) LRA 1925 - protects an actual occupier's interest as an overriding interest against a registered disposition, subject to non-disclosure and not-reasonably-discoverable exceptions.
authorities.verification_note: Confirmed currently in force via a direct legislation.gov.uk fetch on 2026-08-22, independent of the case-law verification above.

edges.verified_via: Link Lending Ltd v Bustard [2010] EWCA Civ 424, fetched directly from Find Case Law: applies Boland's actual-occupation principle.

Link Lending Ltd v Bustard [2010] EWCA Civ 424 discusses LRA 2002 sch 3 para 2 as the statutory successor provision to the one Boland was decided under; the successor text itself was independently confirmed live on legislation.gov.uk.

what_this_is_not: One verified case-to-statute chain confirming the Boland actual-occupation principle transferred intact from the 1925 to the 2002 Act and remains current. Does not independently confirm Boland's original 1980 text, exact decision date, or resolve the AC citation-year discrepancy noted above - see verification_note and citation_note/date_note fields.
